Hello Community,

I have news for the contributors to the Voat code base. We have some needs on Voat right now that will require us to restructure our software on Github in anticipation for the porting of the API.

The bad news is that these actions will most likely break all pending PR requests. Some changes are path related, some are name related, but all need to be done now and not delayed.

A little background:

We were in the middle of a large refactoring before the series of exoduses occurred. Each of these exoduses required performance hacks to ensure Voat would remain running. Keeping two separate code bases and merging between them has proven a complete waste of our time. It's for this reason that we will be addressing issues now rather than later.

What to expect from us

Going forward we will be communicating better with the community about the direction we are taking things. A lot happened all at once and this is new territory for Voat. We both want and need everyone involved to make Voat's code base the best it can be.

For Future Pull Requests (Temporary)

If your PR is not directly addressing an open issue please communicate with us before spending any time working on a large scale refactoring as we have yet to finalize our architectural plans.

Immediate future

We will be developing an entire new component layer from UI to backend (most of which is already written). We will test the API and deploy the API using this new framework. Until then, PRs should be strictly UI based (Voat.UI project) and not include any additional libraries or heavy refactoring.

Backward Compat

All the hacks we have implemented into Voat base for performance/locking reasons are backwards compatible from a project perspective (meaning you will not have to set up SQL Replication to use the project locally). Please be advised though that a new config file with additional settings in it is used.

Thank you guys for all the help. I'm sorry we have to do this.
As someone who runs a large OSS project myself, I understand the need to do this. It's all for the best ultimately! Keep up the good work.
